header: "THIS LOOKS LIKE A NAME": while a person types in the search bar, one to four words that read as an Indian name (or a part of one) earn the hint "Looks like a name. Press Enter to search people", the same way a line that clearly names a utility earns "Looks like <utility>. Press Enter to open it". It is a HINT and nothing more: it changes no search, it never stops one, and it is shown only when no command or utility has claimed the line. I run it in the browser, on every keystroke, with no network and no AI model: a few set look-ups (well under a millisecond). Nothing typed is sent anywhere. I use two sources of knowledge, and each can be switched off (src/lib/search/nameHint/config.ts):
- BUILT-IN: common Indian given names and family names written out in indianNames.ts, and the endings of compound names (Ajaykumar, Gopinath);
- PLANT: the name words of the directory itself (the words only, with nobody attached), fetched once when the search bar opens (/api/employees/name-words).

A word is recognised when it is the same word, or has the same phonetic code (Goutam = Gautam; the code the database itself uses: foldToken), or, for the plant's words only, is one slip away in a spelling-equivalent key (Gosyami -> Goswami: reported as "similar", so the screen can say which word it took it for). Pure.

members.name: words
doc: the name words I read from the line, in upper case, with honorifics and initials left out

members.name: wordCount
doc: the number of words in the line, initials included (the honorific excluded)

members.name: basis
doc: how the words were recognised: I report the WEAKEST basis among them (every word is at least this well known; plant is the strongest, then built-in, then similar spelling)

members.name: similarTo
doc: for a word recognised only by similar spelling: the plant word I took it for, e.g. { typed: "GOSYAMI", took: "GOSWAMI" }

symbols.name: PlantVocab
doc: the plant's words, which I prepare once: the words, their phonetic codes, and the keys of their spelling

members.name: byCode
doc: maps a phonetic code to the words that have it

symbols.name: withoutGlides
doc: W or Y after a consonant and before a vowel is silent in a Bengali name (Goswami = Goshami = Gosyami); I use the same key as src/lib/nl2sql/nameSpelling.ts

symbols.name: codesOf
doc: I take the phonetic code of a word both as a first word and as a last word, because the database compares either

symbols.name: COURTESY_AFTER
doc: words people add after a name that are not part of it

symbols.name: NEVER_NAMES
doc: I never accept these as a name part, even if a vocabulary happens to hold them: they are the words of commands and questions

symbols.name: hasNameEnding
doc: a word of six letters or more that is a known stem plus a known ending (Ajaykumar, Gopinath) I read as a name

symbols.name: slips
symbols.sig: function slips(a: string, b: string, cap: number): number
doc: Returns the number of single-letter slips (insert, delete, change, or swap two neighbours) between two words, or `cap + 1` as soon as it is certain to be more than `cap`

symbols.name: nearSpelling
symbols.sig: const nearSpelling = (word: string, candidates: string[] | undefined): boolean =>
doc: I count a word with the same phonetic code as a known word only if it is also a NEAR spelling of one (same first letter, within 2 letters of its length, a few slips away): the code alone is too loose for ordinary words

symbols.sig: const RANK: Record<NameBasis, number> = { plant: 3, builtin: 2, similar: 1 }

symbols.name: detectNameHint
symbols.sig: export function detectNameHint(line: string, sources: { useBuiltin: boolean; plant: PlantVocab | null }): NameHint | null
doc: The hint for the line typed so far, or null. `useBuiltin` and `plant` are the two sources (either may be off). I treat a line as a name when it has one to four words after any honorific, none with a digit or a symbol, at least one that is not an initial, and EVERY word that is not an initial is recognised.

behaviours: one word of the plant's names, alone
two, three, four words together
capitals and small letters alike
another spelling of the same sound is the same name (Gautam = Goutam, Sandip = Sandeep, Mazumdar = Majumdar)
initials and an honorific are left out: 'G D Kumar', 'Mr Rakesh Ojha', 'Dr. Anita Sharma'
two initials written together (SK, MD) count as initials
a courtesy word after the name is ignored (sir, madam, ji)
a compound name written as one word (Ajaykumar, Gopinath) reads as a name from the built-in endings
the built-in list alone knows the common names (Amit, Sharma, Banerjee) and the plant words alone know the plant's
the basis is the WEAKEST among the words: plant + built-in = built-in
a spelling one slip from a real word, with a silent W or Y, says which word it took it for (Gosyami -> Goswami) and is 'similar'
not a name: "${l}"
a number, a ticket, a P.No., a symbol, a question mark are never a name
more than four words, an empty line, one letter, an honorific alone, initials alone are not a name
the words of commands are never names even if a vocabulary holds them
a line of 61 characters or more is not read
a check costs under a millisecond (measured ${per.toFixed(3)} ms)
foldToken takes 'constructor' and '__proto__' as words
the built-in lists are upper-case letters only, and big enough to matter
no honorific is listed as a name, and no ending that also ends ordinary English words (pal, dev, deb, deep, lal)
the switch has four settings; 'both' uses both sources, 'builtin' fetches nothing, 'plant' uses no built-in names, 'off' uses neither
the shipped setting is one of the four
the search bar shows the hint only when no command, utility, management page or executive mode has the line, and the line has not been searched yet
the plant's words are fetched only when the box is open and the setting uses them
the data route returns the words only (nothing about any person), is limited per address and cached for ten minutes
